brief: Goldman's TMT Today roundup covers five threads. Schneider Electric agreed to buy PTC for about $22.6bn cash, its biggest deal yet, sending PTC up 36% pre-market with ADSK and PCOR rallying in sympathy. Elon Musk confirmed discussions with TSMC about running Terafab's planned Texas chip factories ('just discussions, but something may come of it'); TSM rose on the news while INTC fell 4% on the competitive overhang. GS turns more constructive on semiconductors into Q3 earnings after a two-month pullback (SOX -11% vs SPX +4%) drove de-risking, flagging upside for SemiCap, analog, HDD/NAND and naming AMAT/STX/MCHP as longs against QCOM/KLAC/WDC as shorts; STX and WDC separately fell 10-11% on Toshiba capacity-expansion reports. The S&P 500 Q3 preview expects 27% consensus EPS growth (vs 33% realized in Q2), with AI infrastructure beneficiaries driving over half of that growth and hyperscaler capex up 116%. GS Prime data show net leverage near five-year lows and Russell 2000 positioning in the 7th percentile despite recent short covering, with the desk noting unresolved debate over re-committing to the AI trade given rates, oil and midterm uncertainty.
